rejected.title: Egypt's contact and legacy
card: Egypt traded with neighbours such as Nubia and the Near East. It also fought them, and some of its pharaohs led armies into lands beyond Egypt.

a.q: What is meant by the legacy of ancient Egypt?
opts: What Egypt left behind that people still learn from
The land Egypt won from its neighbours in war
The goods Egypt sold to other peoples in trade
The gods Egyptians worshipped in their temples
a.why: A legacy is what a society leaves behind that later people still use or learn from, such as writing, building and medicine. Conquered land and trade goods belong to Egypt's contact with others, not to what it left behind.
a.clue: Think about what lasts after a society has gone.

b.q: Liam is sorting facts about ancient Egypt under two headings, contact and legacy. Which fact belongs under contact?
opts: Egypt and the Hittites agreed to a peace treaty
Hieroglyphs that scholars can still read today
Stone buildings that people still visit today
Medical texts on papyrus that historians study
b.why: The treaty was an agreement between Egypt and a neighbouring people, so it is part of Egypt's contact with others. Hieroglyphs, stone buildings and medical texts are things Egypt left behind that people still learn from, so they belong under legacy.
b.clue: Which fact is about Egypt dealing with another people?
